public_rationale: Public Meta agreements materially challenge a USD 22 billion ceiling if 'purchases' means multiyear commitments. They do not settle a ceiling on actual spending over an unspecified period. The Nebius headline also includes conditional capacity. The claim's accounting basis is unknown, so these company-reported commitments cannot be promoted to matching outcome evidence. A categorical verdict would depend on a financial definition the speaker did not supply.
limitations: This assesses the public-evidence implication, not the contents of the author's private search.
Contract face values are not annual revenue, annual spending or payments already made.
The available examples establish identifiable commitments, not a complete market total.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Despite looking everywhere, Zitron has found at the very best $22 billion of compute purchases by buyers other than OpenAI and Anthropic.

statement.excerpt: I’ve looked everywhere and I’ve found at the very, very best $22 billion of non-OpenAI/Anthropic compute purchases!

from_speaker: at the very, very best $22 billion
our_interpretation: Read this as a public-evidence claim about identifiable AI compute purchases, rather than an unverifiable claim about the author's private search history.

The search universe ends at publication. Because the statement concerns what has been found and supplies no starting date, use an open-start period ending October 6 rather than invent an annual spending window.
The ordinary reading identifies buyers other than OpenAI and Anthropic. It does not specify whether intermediary purchases ultimately serving those companies are excluded.
The words do not distinguish completed purchases, annual spending and multiyear contractual commitments. These measures will not be treated as interchangeable.
The dollar sign is read as US dollars. No cited company figures, press estimate or accounting basis are identified in the supplied wording.
criteria.support_condition: A documented and sufficiently complete inventory, using a stated purchase measure and consistent time basis, establishes that identifiable purchases by the eligible buyers total no more than USD 22 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A non-overlapping set of eligible purchases exceeds USD 22 billion on the same purchase, accounting and time basis as the claim.

evidence.explanation: The announcement identifies approximately USD 21 billion of contracted AI cloud capacity for Meta through December 2032. It is relevant to identifiable demand but does not measure realized purchases in an unspecified spending period.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following the dedicated-capacity and additional-capacity descriptions
evidence.explanation: The announcement separates USD 12 billion of dedicated capacity from up to USD 15 billion of additional capacity that Meta would purchase if other customers did not. The headline maximum is not realized spending or an unconditional USD 27 billion purchase.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: The calculation behind USD 22 billion, including its period, accounting basis, eligible buyers and treatment of commitments, followed by a non-overlapping comparison using that same measure.
